_what: Every leaf path the frozen number table carries, the blocks and map-row keys it must hold, and the ONLY leaves permitted to be null. verify.py requires all of them, in both directions, and refuses to run unless this file's SHA-256 and its four cardinalities match constants compiled into verify.py itself. That last clause is the point: a declaration file that merely has to AGREE with the two number tables is a third mutually-trusting surface, not an anchor -- v59 shipped exactly that, and a size-preserving edit of all three returned a global PASS after deleting 29 of 47 blocks and 11 of 12 map-row keys. Editing this file alone now fails on the digest; editing it together with verify.py's constants is a source change to the reviewed artifact, which is what review is for. This does NOT make omission impossible -- it makes it a code edit rather than a data edit. Nothing here binds verify.py itself.
